title: Impact of Obesity Diagnosis on Medication Use

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Sharp (or fuzzy, if needed) Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) at the BMI cutoff. Individuals just above the obesity threshold (treated) are compared to those just below it (control) using local polynomial regressions with triangular kernel weights.
- Why: Treatment (diagnosis) turns on at a known threshold in the running variable (BMI). The sample is focused around the cutoff, making RD the natural design.
- Key assumptions:
  - Continuity: In the absence of diagnosis, the conditional expectation of log medication use would be continuous in BMI at the cutoff.
  - No precise manipulation: Individuals cannot precisely sort their BMI around the cutoff.
  - Sharp compliance: Treatment equals the indicator of crossing the cutoff. If small deviations exist, we switch to fuzzy RD where the discontinuity in treatment at the cutoff serves as an instrument for actual treatment.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code that:
# - Reads the CSV file from the path provided
# - Runs the appropriate causal analysis
# - Prints a clear numerical result (coefficient, CAR, etc.)
# - Includes basic robustness checks

# Setup
options(scipen = 999, digits = 4)

pkgs <- c("sandwich", "lmtest")
for (p in pkgs) {
  if (!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) install.packages(p, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
  library(p, character.only = TRUE)
}
# Optional packages for fuzzy RD and density test
if (!requireNamespace("AER", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("AER", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
library(AER)
has_rddensity <- requireNamespace("rddensity", quietly = TRUE)
if (has_rddensity) library(rddensity)

# Read data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s100_data.csv")

# Basic checks
stopifnot(all(c("running_var", "treated", "y") %in% names(df)))
df <- subset(df, is.finite(running_var) & is.finite(treated) & is.finite(y))

# Define cutoff (consistent with treated indicator preview)
c0 <- 0.5
x  <- df$running_var
D  <- df$treated
y  <- df$y

# Check sharpness (perfect compliance with cutoff)
mis <- sum(D != as.integer(x >= c0), na.rm = TRUE)
cat("Treatment misclassification relative to cutoff:", mis, "of", nrow(df), "\n")
is_sharp <- (mis == 0)

# Helper: local linear RD (sharp)
sharp_rd <- function(y, x, D, c, h, p = 1, donut = 0) {
  rx <- x - c
  keep <- (abs(rx) <= h) & (abs(rx) > donut)
  if (sum(keep) < 30 || length(unique(D[keep])) < 2) {
    return(list(tau = NA, se = NA, n = sum(keep)))
  }
  rx <- rx[keep]; Dk <- D[keep]; yk <- y[keep]
  # Triangular weights
  w <- (1 - abs(rx) / h); w[w < 0] <- 0

  # Polynomial terms
  X <- cbind(1, Dk, rx, Dk * rx)
  colnames(X) <- c("const", "D", "rx", "D_rx")
  if (p >= 2) {
    rx2 <- rx^2
    X <- cbind(X, rx2, Dk * rx2)
    colnames(X)[(ncol(X)-1):ncol(X)] <- c("rx2", "D_rx2")
  }

  fit <- lm(yk ~ 0 + X, weights = w)
  vc <- sandwich::vcovHC(fit, type = "HC1")
  coefs <- coef(fit)
  se <- sqrt(diag(vc))
  tau <- unname(coefs["XD"])
  se_tau <- unname(se["XD"])
  t <- tau / se_tau
  pval <- 2 * pnorm(-abs(t))
  ci_lo <- tau - 1.96 * se_tau
  ci_hi <- tau + 1.96 * se_tau
  list(tau = tau, se = se_tau, t = t, p = pval, ci = c(ci_lo, ci_hi), n = sum(keep), h = h, porder = p, donut = donut)
}

# Helper: local linear RD (fuzzy) via 2SLS with same local polynomial and instruments
fuzzy_rd <- function(y, x, D, c, h, p = 1, donut = 0) {
  rx <- x - c
  Z  <- as.integer(x >= c)
  keep <- (abs(rx) <= h) & (abs(rx) > donut)
  if (sum(keep) < 30 || length(unique(Z[keep])) < 2) {
    return(list(tau = NA, se = NA, n = sum(keep)))
  }
  rx <- rx[keep]; Dk <- D[keep]; yk <- y[keep]; Zk <- Z[keep]
  w <- (1 - abs(rx) / h); w[w < 0] <- 0

  # Build formulas allowing different slopes
  dat <- data.frame(y = yk, D = Dk, Z = Zk, rx = rx)
  if (p == 1) {
    form <- y ~ D + rx + D:rx | Z + rx + Z:rx
    target_coef <- "D"
  } else {
    dat$rx2 <- rx^2
    form <- y ~ D + rx + D:rx + I(rx^2) + D:I(rx^2) | Z + rx + Z:rx + I(rx^2) + Z:I(rx^2)
    target_coef <- "D"
  }
  fit_iv <- AER::ivreg(form, data = dat, weights = w)
  vc <- sandwich::vcovHC(fit_iv, type = "HC1")
  ct <- lmtest::coeftest(fit_iv, vcov. = vc)
  if (!(target_coef %in% rownames(ct))) {
    return(list(tau = NA, se = NA, n = sum(keep)))
  }
  tau <- unname(ct[target_coef, "Estimate"])
  se  <- unname(ct[target_coef, "Std. Error"])
  t   <- unname(ct[target_coef, "t value"])
  pval <- unname(ct[target_coef, "Pr(>|t|)"])
  ci_lo <- tau - 1.96 * se
  ci_hi <- tau + 1.96 * se
  list(tau = tau, se = se, t = t, p = pval, ci = c(ci_lo, ci_hi), n = sum(keep), h = h, porder = p, donut = donut)
}

# Choose a baseline bandwidth (simple, then verify robustness)
range_x <- diff(range(x, na.rm = TRUE))
h_base <- 0.15 * range_x
h_base <- max(h_base, 0.05 * range_x)  # avoid too small
h_half <- 0.5 * h_base
h_double <- min(2 * h_base, 0.5 * range_x) # avoid too wide

# Main estimate
if (is_sharp) {
  main <- sharp_rd(y, x, D, c0, h = h_base, p = 1, donut = 0)
  cat("\nMain SHARP RD (local linear, triangular kernel)\n")
} else {
  main <- fuzzy_rd(y, x, D, c0, h = h_base, p = 1, donut = 0)
  cat("\nMain FUZZY RD (local linear 2SLS, triangular kernel)\n")
}
cat(sprintf("Cutoff = %.3f, h = %.3f, n = %d\n", c0, main$h, main$n))
cat(sprintf("Local treatment effect on log medication use: %.4f\n", main$tau))
cat(sprintf("Std. Error: %.4f | p-value: %.4f | 95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
            main$se, main$p, main$ci[1], main$ci[2]))

# Naive local difference-in-means within a tiny window (diagnostic only)
eps <- 0.025 * range_x
near <- abs(x - c0) <= eps
if (sum(near & D == 1) >= 5 && sum(near & D == 0) >= 5) {
  dm <- mean(y[near & D == 1]) - mean(y[near & D == 0])
  cat(sprintf("\nNaive diff-in-means within |BMI - cutoff| <= %.3f: %.4f (n = %d)\n",
              eps, dm, sum(near)))
}

# Manipulation / density test at cutoff (if available)
if (has_rddensity) {
  dens <- try(rddensity::rddensity(X = x, c = c0), silent = TRUE)
  if (!inherits(dens, "try-error")) {
    cat("\nMcCrary density test at cutoff (rddensity):\n")
    print(rddensity::summary.rddensity(dens))
  }
}

# Robustness checks
robust_results <- list()

# 1) Bandwidth sensitivity (half, double)
if (is_sharp) {
  rb_hhalf <- sharp_rd(y, x, D, c0, h = h_half, p = 1)
  rb_hdbl  <- sharp_rd(y, x, D, c0, h = h_double, p = 1)
} else {
  rb_hhalf <- fuzzy_rd(y, x, D, c0, h = h_half, p = 1)
  rb_hdbl  <- fuzzy_rd(y, x, D, c0, h = h_double, p = 1)
}
robust_results$h_half <- rb_hhalf
robust_results$h_double <- rb_hdbl

cat("\nBandwidth sensitivity:\n")
cat(sprintf("h/2 effect: %.4f (se=%.4f, p=%.4f, n=%d)\n",
            rb_hhalf$tau, rb_hhalf$se, rb_hhalf$p, rb_hhalf$n))
cat(sprintf("2h  effect: %.4f (se=%.4f, p=%.4f, n=%d)\n",
            rb_hdbl$tau,  rb_hdbl$se,  rb_hdbl$p,  rb_hdbl$n))

# 2) Polynomial order: local quadratic
if (is_sharp) {
  rb_p2 <- sharp_rd(y, x, D, c0, h = h_base, p = 2)
} else {
  rb_p2 <- fuzzy_rd(y, x, D, c0, h = h_base, p = 2)
}
robust_results$p2 <- rb_p2
cat("\nLocal quadratic (p=2):\n")
cat(sprintf("Effect: %.4f (se=%.4f, p=%.4f, n=%d)\n",
            rb_p2$tau, rb_p2$se, rb_p2$p, rb_p2$n))

# 3) Donut hole: drop very near the cutoff (avoid heaping)
donut <- 0.01 * range_x
if (is_sharp) {
  rb_donut <- sharp_rd(y, x, D, c0, h = h_base, p = 1, donut = donut)
} else {
  rb_donut <- fuzzy_rd(y, x, D, c0, h = h_base, p = 1, donut = donut)
}
robust_results$donut <- rb_donut
cat("\nDonut (exclude |x-c| <=", sprintf("%.3f", donut), "):\n")
cat(sprintf("Effect: %.4f (se=%.4f, p=%.4f, n=%d)\n",
            rb_donut$tau, rb_donut$se, rb_donut$p, rb_donut$n))

# 4) Placebo cutoff
c_placebo <- 0.6
if (is_sharp) {
  rb_placebo <- sharp_rd(y, x, D = as.integer(x >= c_placebo), c = c_placebo, h = h_base, p = 1)
} else {
  rb_placebo <- fuzzy_rd(y, x, D, c = c_placebo, h = h_base, p = 1)
}
robust_results$placebo <- rb_placebo
cat("\nPlacebo cutoff at 0.600 (should be ~0 if design valid):\n")
cat(sprintf("Effect: %.4f (se=%.4f, p=%.4f, n=%d)\n",
            rb_placebo$tau, rb_placebo$se, rb_placebo$p, rb_placebo$n))

# 5) Restrict to near-cutoff subsample (if provided)
if ("near_cutoff" %in% names(df)) {
  sub <- df[df$near_cutoff == 1, ]
  if (nrow(sub) >= 50) {
    x2 <- sub$running_var; D2 <- sub$treated; y2 <- sub$y
    range_x2 <- diff(range(x2, na.rm = TRUE))
    h_sub <- max(0.15 * range_x2, 0.05 * range_x2)
    if (is_sharp) {
      rb_near <- sharp_rd(y2, x2, D2, c0, h = h_sub, p = 1)
    } else {
      rb_near <- fuzzy_rd(y2, x2, D2, c0, h = h_sub, p = 1)
    }
    robust_results$near <- rb_near
    cat("\nEstimate on near-cutoff subsample:\n")
    cat(sprintf("h=%.3f | Effect: %.4f (se=%.4f, p=%.4f, n=%d)\n",
                rb_near$h, rb_near$tau, rb_near$se, rb_near$p, rb_near$n))
  }
}

cat("\nDone.\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive. Being (just) diagnosed as obese should increase subsequent medication use via increased physician attention, guideline-triggered prescribing (e.g., for cardiometabolic risk), and patient salience.
- Magnitude: On log medication use, a local effect around 0.10–0.30 is plausible, implying roughly 10–35% higher medication use just above the cutoff versus just below. The exact magnitude depends on how tightly medication decisions are tied to the diagnosis near the threshold and sample composition. Robustness checks should show stability across bandwidths/polynomials and no discontinuity at placebo cutoffs.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare medication use for individuals just above and below the BMI cutoff.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Receiving an obesity diagnosis at the BMI cutoff leads to increased medication use.
